result:
I made the fix. Type-checking passes, and so do the 9 existing tests in `tests/lib/feature-flags.test.ts`. I didn't run the rest of the test suite or add any new tests.

**1. Switching an override off didn't stick.** The general org-update function (`updateOrg` in `src/server/repositories/organization-repository.ts`) always merged the new list of overrides into the stored one. So a removed override came straight back. That merge is deliberate: the org settings form always sends an empty override list, and without the merge, saving the form would wipe every override. So I left it alone and added a separate function, `setFlagOverrides`, which writes the complete list as given. The feature-switch code now uses it, so switching one override off removes just that one and leaves the others. Switching it on again works too.

**2. Features that aren't overridable could be switched on anyway.**
- **Rejecting the request:** the check in `src/server/services/feature-flag-service.ts` let any plan-based feature through, so I changed it to reject every feature marked not overridable. I also added the same check at the start of the action in `src/actions/flags/toggle-flag.ts`. Without it, a request that wouldn't change the result (such as turning webhooks on for a workspace whose plan already includes them) would report success. Now all such requests fail with an error and nothing is stored.
- **Ignoring stored overrides:** `isEnabled` in `src/lib/feature-flags.ts` now only honours an override if the feature is overridable. Otherwise the feature is decided by its own rule (e.g. the plan), even if an override is already saved in the workspace's settings. Overridable features behave as before.
